rationale: All required child capabilities now exist as independently verified repository-local components. A one-shot read-only orchestrator can be built primarily by composing their public verification and deterministic generation contracts, while preserving exact fingerprints and without introducing scheduling, provider, adjacent-repository write, Skill mutation, or approval authority. The main remaining work is integration, a canonical loop-run schema, source-drift detection, and focused fail-closed tests.

queries: current read-only loop verifier deterministic recommendation checkpoint
governed execution controller local dry-run execution record authorization
outcome evidence regression rollback learning proposal exact fingerprints
FREEZER WIP preflight lifecycle manifest integration

assets.notes: Pins the current cross-repository asset inventory without copying adjacent repository bodies.
Provides deterministic observation, evaluation, recommendation, and read-only checkpoint semantics.
Provides bounded local execution-record, authorization, budget, checkpoint, and emergency-stop contracts without requiring live provider authority.
Provides privacy-safe governed outcome bundles, evidence integrity, and classification verification.
Provides deterministic baseline/candidate regression, thresholds, result fingerprints, and rollback snapshot verification.
Provides proposal-only generation, pending human review, exact provenance, and fail-closed authority boundaries.
Canonical minimal execution result contract for one-shot loop linkage.
Canonical evidence reference contract for reconstructable loop records.
Supplies Assessment, Preflight, WIP=1, append-only lifecycle, and manifest verification gates.

gaps: No current loop-run schema binds all component fingerprints into one canonical record.
No current one-shot CLI invokes the completed component verification contracts in a fixed order.
Current committed outcomes are SIMULATED_ONLY and cannot establish external business or user success.
The first version must not schedule itself, call providers, write adjacent repositories, approve proposals, or apply Skills.
Human Review Ledger and Promotion Application Preview remain separate future children.

risks: Integration could silently bypass a child verifier and accept stale fingerprints.
A loop-run record could accidentally persist private prompts, credentials, customer data, provider payloads, or repository bodies.
Calling the execution controller could be misread as permission for live provider execution rather than bounded local record composition.
A proposal output could be mistaken for human approval or Skill-application authority.
Future scheduling or cross-repository adapters could be added without a separate Assessment, Preflight, and approval gate.
